document.title: Ambassador Dean Cable, "Subject: Gandhi's visit to Moscow"
document.authors: Ambassador John Gunther Dean, U.S. Embassy New Delhi
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Dean reports on Indian officials' accounts of Gandhi's Moscow stopover. Gandhi focused on disarmament and Pakistan's nuclear bomb with Gorbachev, and regretted that the U.S. would not talk about guarantees after a Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan.

events.description: Rajiv Gandhi returned to New Delhi after a stopover in Moscow meeting Gorbachev.
Rajiv Gandhi met Gorbachev in Moscow, discussing disarmament, Pakistan's nuclear program, and Afghanistan.
Gandhi met President Reagan in New York.
Bhandari held meetings with Soviet leadership following Rajiv's Washington visit.
Rajiv Gandhi returned to New Delhi from Moscow; Ambassador Dean welcomed him at the airport.
Rajiv Gandhi stopped over in Moscow and met Gorbachev, discussing disarmament, Pakistan's nuclear program, China and Afghanistan.
Gorbachev shortened his Sofia stay by 24 hours, making the Moscow stopover possible; word came one hour before Gandhi left the Netherlands.
Ambassador Dean sent cable analyzing Gandhi's Moscow visit.

sources_cited: Rajiv Gandhi homecoming press conference 27 Oct 1985
key_claims: Initiative for the Moscow stopover reportedly came from Rajiv Gandhi.
Gandhi stressed disarmament and his certainty that Pakistan was building a nuclear bomb.
Gandhi raised Afghanistan, saying the US was unwilling to discuss guarantees after Soviet withdrawal; Dean thinks Rajiv misunderstood the US position.
Dean fears Indian media portray Gorbachev's policies as closer to India's than Reagan's.
The British High Commissioner thought Afghanistan was not discussed in depth since Bhandari stayed in New York.
